key_insight: A variance-reduced primal-dual method supports multiple local updates with a stepsize independent of network size and inversely proportional to the number of local updates, while guaranteeing linear convergence in expectation under strong convexity.
engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate decentralized stochastic optimization while exchanging only one variable per round, halving communication cost relative to gradient-tracking-based methods.
method: Combine a decentralized primal-dual algorithm with stochastic variance reduction.
Perform multiple local updates between communication rounds.
Improve allowable stepsize scaling from inverse-cubic to inverse-linear in local update count.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees and numerical experiments showing faster convergence and improved accuracy, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The linear convergence guarantee assumes strong convexity and should not be generalized to nonconvex objectives.
paper_title: Variance Reduction for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Multiple Local Updates
